Reports from the former Bourbon mainland describe armed bands, legitimist networks and resistance to conscription and taxation. Agrarian grievances and local rivalries overlap with political opposition. The cabinet must choose how to establish royal authority without treating every dispute as the same rebellion.
The emergency in the South has prompted a proposal for military jurisdiction and exceptional police powers in designated districts. Supporters promise to disrupt armed networks
column3: opponents warn that arbitrary arrests and collective suspicion will deepen hostility. Civil reconciliation remains an alternative.

column2: Retain ordinary jurisdiction and local commissions.

The exceptional legislative period is drawing to a close. Armed opposition has not made every southern grievance identical, and the return to ordinary administration cannot by itself resolve land disputes, poverty or distrust of officials.

Roma o Morte: The Crown and the Volunteers

Volunteer agitation in Calabria threatens to carry the Roman question beyond the cabinet's control. The Papal government still holds Rome and France remains a powerful protector. Ministers must decide whether to stop an unauthorized expedition or tolerate preparations that could provoke a diplomatic crisis.
Roma o Morte: The Crown and the Volunteers: concluded
Roma o Morte: The Crown and the Volunteers: presented

Offer France a pledge to respect and defend the remaining Papal territory in return for withdrawal of its expeditionary presence. The proposed understanding includes removing the capital from Turin to Florence. Paris must accept before the arrangement can proceed.
Negotiate a Convention on Rome: enacted

The Italian cabinet proposes a convention over the remaining Papal territory and offers to transfer its capital to Florence. Acceptance would commit France to withdraw its expeditionary presence while Italy undertakes not to attack the Pope and to defend his territory.
An Italian Proposal on Rome: concluded
An Italian Proposal on Rome: presented

Paris has accepted the proposed understanding on Rome. Italy has undertaken to respect the remaining Papal territory, and the transfer of the ministries to Florence must now be prepared. The agreement addresses military protection
column3: it does not resolve the Pope's objection to Italian unity.

column2: Paris has declined the proposed understanding. There is no agreed French withdrawal and no obligation arising from these negotiations to move the ministries. The Roman question remains open.

The negotiations with France have ended without a binding settlement. Changes in the diplomatic situation or the failure to secure a timely response have left the proposed exchange of undertakings unratified.
The Roman Negotiations Have Lapsed: concluded
The Roman Negotiations Have Lapsed: presented

Prepare Florence to receive the court, parliament and central ministries under the convention with France. Turin faces the loss of employment and influence associated with the capital, while the receiving city must accommodate the national administration.
Transfer the Capital to Florence: enacted
Turin and the Departure of the Ministries

The decision to remove the ministries has provoked anger in Turin. Trades dependent on the court face disruption, while critics condemn the manner in which the agreement was reached. The cabinet must answer demands for an inquiry and assistance to the city.
Turin and the Departure of the Ministries: concluded
Turin and the Departure of the Ministries: presented
Permit an inquiry and municipal relief.
Defend the authority of the cabinet.

The agreed period for French withdrawal has elapsed. Parliament must decide whether to uphold the pledge over Papal territory or openly renounce it. Even a withdrawal does not prevent France from intervening again if its government chooses to defend the Pope.
The conditions on which the Roman convention rested have changed. The cabinet can no longer administer the old undertaking as though the military and territorial situation were unchanged.
The Convention Loses Its Basis: concluded
The Convention Loses Its Basis: presented
Record the end of the undertaking.
Replace the inherited civil systems with common rules for property, contracts and family law. This programme concerns civil administration
column3: the distinct Tuscan criminal settlement is not abolished by it.

The common civil code is ready for administration across the kingdom. Courts and officials now share a legal framework, though uniform legislation does not eliminate the practical differences between local institutions.
The Civil Code Enters into Force: concluded
The Civil Code Enters into Force: presented

The alliance with Prussia has committed Italy to a war against Austria over Venetia. Diplomatic cooperation may divide Austrian strength, but the army must still conduct its campaign and the final settlement remains uncertain.

War expenditure and pressure on reserves have brought the question of compulsory paper circulation before the cabinet. Suspending convertibility would ease the immediate financing strain, but savers and households would bear uncertainty over the value of money. The kingdom still has several banks of issue.
Provide a common supply service for the campaign against Austria. The undertaking supports operations
column3: possession of Venetia will depend on the war and the peace settlement.

Venice and its mainland districts have passed under Italian sovereignty. The task now is to reconcile their administration with the kingdom and to give the settlement a public constitutional expression. Acquisition of the territory does not settle every claim along the Alpine frontier.
Venetia Under the Italian Crown: concluded
Venetia Under the Italian Crown: presented
Ratify the union and establish civil authority.

Peace has brought the campaign before parliament. Separate commands, supply arrangements and relations between the army and fleet require examination. The inquiry must assess the forces actually employed, without mistaking diplomatic gains for proof that every institution worked well.
Leave the review to the royal command.
Establish common staff procedures, tactical instruction and gunnery training across the fleet. The navy inherited different service traditions
column3: a new organization must be supported by sustained training rather than ceremonial unity alone.

The funded programme has completed its first cycle of staff instruction and gunnery training. Common procedures now support the fleet, while actual readiness continues to depend on crews, ships and the naval budget.

The Naval Reform Programme Reports: presented

Reports from Palermo describe unrest drawing on poverty, hostility to conscription and taxation, and resentment of central authority. Republicans, clerical interests and Bourbon sympathizers do not share one programme. The ministry must decide between emergency policing and a negotiated municipal response.
Palermo: The Crisis of September: concluded
Palermo: The Crisis of September: presented

A new movement to advance on Rome is gathering support. The Papal state survives, and France retains the ability to intervene. The cabinet can restrain the volunteers or tolerate agitation at the cost of its diplomatic assurances. The fate of any actual campaign will be decided on the ground.

The treasury seeks dependable revenue to meet the obligations of the new kingdom. A duty collected at the mill would reach the consumption of basic grain products and provoke opposition among poorer households. A more direct assessment of property would place the dispute elsewhere and yield less immediately.
The New Assessments Enter into Force

The new fiscal legislation is entering administration. Collectors must enforce it through local institutions, where objections to the distribution of the burden can become a broader dispute with the state.
The New Assessments Enter into Force: concluded
The New Assessments Enter into Force: presented
Withdraw the duty on milling and relinquish its revenue. The decision can ease the burden on basic consumption, but leaves the cabinet to meet its obligations through the ordinary budget.
Provide support for municipal schools and teacher preparation in the united kingdom. A wider network requires local staff and sustained finance
column3: literacy will improve through education rather than by decree.

column2: The funded programme has expanded the capacity of municipalities to maintain primary instruction. Recruitment and attendance remain uneven, but the state can now support education through a broader network.
The Municipal School Programme Reports: concluded

Back an exploratory commercial mission for Rubattino near Assab. A private coaling contract might serve shipping through Suez, but negotiations with local authorities and competing claims must precede any permanent establishment.

Representatives of an Italian shipping company seek a private establishment near Assab. A contract would concern commercial access and local property
column3: it would not transfer sovereignty over the surrounding province to the Italian state.

Rubattino's agents report agreement for a private commercial establishment near Assab. The undertaking remains vulnerable to rival jurisdictional claims and insecure access. Its existence does not make Assab a colony of the Italian state.
A Private Contract at Assab: concluded
A Private Contract at Assab: presented
Keep the venture on a commercial footing.

The proposed commercial establishment has met obstruction or failed to obtain an effective agreement. The government must distinguish a private company's ambitions from rights it can actually enforce.
The Assab Venture Faces Obstruction: concluded
The Assab Venture Faces Obstruction: presented
Record the failure of the proposal.
Assab and the Limits of Private Expansion

The commercial venture has not provided a secure basis for state authority in the Red Sea. Rival claims and the cost of maintaining access remain obstacles. A future government would need a distinct agreement before assuming sovereignty.
Assab and the Limits of Private Expansion: concluded
Assab and the Limits of Private Expansion: presented
An Opening in the Roman Question

France's diminished ability to protect the Papal state has reopened the Roman question. Ministers can prepare a claim to the remaining Papal territory or continue diplomacy. Neither course itself determines possession of Rome.
An Opening in the Roman Question: concluded
An Opening in the Roman Question: presented

Authorize the army to enter the remaining Papal territory after France's protective position has weakened. Rome must be secured through the campaign and its settlement. Other powers remain free to respond through their alliances.

Rome is now under Italian sovereignty and the fighting has ended. The civil administration must establish its authority while the Pope contests the loss of temporal power. Public ratification can confirm the national settlement without resolving the religious dispute.
Ratify the union and establish civil authority.

Transfer parliament, the court and central ministries to Rome. Preparing offices and accommodating the national administration requires a separate undertaking from the settlement of the Pope's legal position.
Establish the Capital at Rome: enacted

Offer statutory guarantees for the Pope's person, spiritual functions and diplomatic relations. This is a unilateral Italian law, not a concordat: the Holy See may continue to reject the loss of temporal sovereignty.
Enact the Law of Guarantees: enacted
The Holy See Rejects a Unilateral Settlement

The Holy See rejects the view that Italian legislation can settle its claim to temporal sovereignty. The guarantees remain the law of the kingdom, but the Roman Question continues. The Pope's religious authority does not depend on possessing a government represented on the political map.
The Holy See Rejects a Unilateral Settlement: concluded
The Holy See Rejects a Unilateral Settlement: presented
Maintain the guarantees despite the dispute.
The Convention and French Protection of Rome

Italy has transferred its capital to Florence and the agreed interval has elapsed. France must now decide whether to end its formal military and diplomatic protection of the remaining Papal state or retain it despite the undertaking.
The Convention and French Protection of Rome: concluded
The Convention and French Protection of Rome: presented

France has ended its formal alliance and access arrangements with the Papal government and relinquished its sphere claim where applicable. Italy remains bound by its own non-intervention pledge. A future French government can still choose to intervene again.
France Ends Its Protective Commitment: concluded
France Ends Its Protective Commitment: presented
France Retains Protection of the Pope

France has declined to end its protective commitment despite the convention and the transfer to Florence. The cabinet can continue to seek compliance or renounce its own undertaking. Renunciation does not itself secure Rome.
France Retains Protection of the Pope: concluded
France Retains Protection of the Pope: presented
